title: Microburst spectrogram comparative notes
body:
Summary:
This note collects an informal, visual-first comparison of microburst shapes across session cohorts using a "spectrogram"-style ASCII visualization. Goal: surface differences in burst frequency, amplitude, and cost impact (dollars/token) between workload cohorts and runtime knobs (tiling vs prefetch, smallbatch vs dynbatch). Output is a working sketch for a future one-pager and a canonical benchmark harness ticket.

Setup notes (quick):
- Date: 2027-09-21 to 2027-09-28
- Clusters: two test pools (core-us-east-1 c5-like + edge-eu-west shard) isolated by tag
- Models: open-llama-13B (fp16), llama-13B-quant4 (Q4), and a trimmed 6B variant (fp16)
- Traffic generator: replayed production session traces (sampled 0.5%) with injected synthetic microbursts at random offsets to test tail behavior
- Knobs toggled: tiling on/off, prefix KV cache enabled/disabled, batch mode smallbatch/dynbatch, handshake timeout 120ms/300ms
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 latency, token/second throughput, per-request $ estimate (simple model: gpu-costs amortized + infra egress), slot utilization

High-level takeaways (draft):
- Cohort A (interactive search sessions, short priming, many tiny bursts) shows high burst frequency but low amplitude. Tiling + KV cache reduces p99 by ~18% vs baseline; smallbatch helps p50 but increases p99 slightly when tiling is off.
- Cohort B (long-form editing, sustained generation punctuated by microbursts) has lower burst frequency but higher amplitude; prefetch/tiling combos improve throughput and reduce $/k tokens by ~12% for Q4 runs.
- Edge shards (eu-west) show slightly higher median latencies (10-15ms) due to networking but improved tail in some combos because of lower multiplexing pressure.

Compact ASCII spectrogram (cohort A) — each column = 20s time bin, rows = burst amplitude class (H/M/L). Character density approximates frequency in bin.
Time bins: [T0][T1][T2][T3][T4][T5][T6][T7]
H | ###   ##    ##   #    ###   ##   #    #
M | #### ####  ####  ###  ####  ###  ##   ##
L | ##########  ########  ##### ##### #### ####

Interpretation: lots of low-amplitude activity, occasional high spikes. Compare to Cohort B:
H | #####    ####    ######    ####
M | ###      ###     ####     ###
L | #######  #####   ######   ####

This shows fewer columns with H amplitude but when present they last across bins (sustained).

Latency / cost sketch table (text):
Model | Knob set | p50 (ms) | p99 (ms) | tokens/sec | est $/1k tokens
open-13B fp16 | tiling+cache | 85 | 320 | 200 | $0.045
open-13B fp16 | no-tiling | 72 | 410 | 240 | $0.052
llama-13B q4   | tiling+cache | 110 | 380 | 420 | $0.026
6B trimmed fp16 | tiling | 48 | 270 | 550 | $0.037

Notes on the table: the Q4 runs have higher per-request latency but much lower $/k tokens because of higher throughput — useful for dedicated-mode cost arguments. p99 sensitivity to tiling being off grows most for fp16 13B (likely kernel-path and memory churn).

Mini chart: p99 delta (no-tiling -> tiling+cache) for cohort A by model:
open-13B fp16: -90ms
llama-13B q4: -30ms
6B fp16: -40ms

Unresolved questions / weird signals:
- We saw an anomalous p99 bump on the edge shard between T3-T4 when handshake timeout was 300ms; hypothesis: idle conn reuse + client retry storms. Need to correlate with handshake logs (ENGOBS-3421).
- Smallbatch improved p50 broadly but in a minority of traces increased p99; looks like adversarial mixing of long sessions and tiny bursts causing batch starvation. Could be handled via hybrid admission or per-tenant pacing.

Next steps / action items:
- Turn this sketch into a reproducible lab: capture a minimized harness that replays only the anomalous sequences (Samir) — ticket GH #218 points at the harness.
- Add spectrogram heatmap exporter (PNG + CSV) to the observability harness; use the ASCII as fallback for docs.
- Run a controlled Q4 vs FP16 head-to-head at scale for dedicated pool sizing; product ask: quantify tail vs price for a 99th percentile SLA.
- Draft a one-pager summarizing when recommending Q4 vs FP16 to customers across three usage profiles (microburst-heavy mobile search, long-form drafting, embeddings-heavy batch).

Raw quicklinks / traces to check later:
- sample trace id: trace-us-east-7f9a2b (see trace logs in s3/test-replay bucket)
- harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/218
- ticket: JIRA ENGOBS-3421

Notes-to-self: keep ASCII spectrogram idea — it's a compact way to show burst frequency + amplitude in a single glance for slide decks. Consider encoding color bands in the console text renderer."
